entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
The Computer History Museum, founded in 1996 and located in Mountain View, California, stands as a pivotal institution dedicated to preserving the artifacts and narratives surrounding the evolution of computing. This museum occupies a significant space in the history of technology, showcasing the innovations that have transformed the way we communicate, work, and think. Key figures in the development of computing, such as Alan Turing, Ada Lovelace, and Steve Jobs, are represented through exhibits that chronicle the journey from early mechanical calculators to modern artificial intelligence, thereby highlighting the profound impact of these advancements on society and culture.

Key milestones at the Computer History Museum include the acquisition of the original Apple I computer in 2013, and the establishment of the "Revolution: The First 2000 Years of Computing" exhibit, which presents a comprehensive narrative of computing history from ancient times to the present. The museum not only offers a glimpse into technological breakthroughs but also serves as an educational platform through its hands-on exhibits and programs, fostering a deeper understanding of the role of computing in contemporary life. With over 1,000 artifacts and numerous interactive displays, it effectively narrates the complex story of how computers have become integral to almost every aspect of modern existence.
